panels.title: Devices
panels.description: Counts come from the main router's AiMesh client list, so every node is included.

panels.title: Wi-Fi
panels.description: Wi-Fi devices on every node and SSID.

panels.title: Wired
panels.description: Devices on an Ethernet port of the router or a mesh node.

panels.title: Guest network
panels.description: Devices on an SSID with "guest" in its name.

panels.title: DHCP leases
panels.description: Leases include devices that left recently, so this is usually higher than Devices.

panels.title: All devices
panels.description: One row per device. Click a MAC for its details page. Filter a column with the funnel icon in its header. Counts come from the main router's AiMesh client list, so every node is included.

targets.expr: asus_client_rssi_dbm * on (mac) group_left (ip, vendor, owner, type) asus_client_info

panels.title: Wired devices
panels.description: Devices behind a mesh node show under that node, not the main router.

panels.title: New devices (24h)
panels.description: Devices the collector had never seen before. The collector's first poll after a fresh install is the baseline, so those devices don't count.

panels.title: Roams (24h)
panels.description: Moves to another mesh node or band while connected.

panels.title: Known devices offline
panels.description: Seen in the last CLIENT_RETENTION_DAYS days but not connected now.

panels.title: Recent roams (24h)
panels.description: The latest roam of each device that roamed in the past day.

panels.title: Last seen
panels.description: Every device seen in the retention window, online or not.

panels.title: Online timeline
panels.description: Named devices only (name them in the Asus app or devices.yml).

panels.title: Wi-Fi link details (from each node's radios)
Wi-Fi link details
panels.description: Link rate and traffic per Wi-Fi device, read with `wl` on each node that accepts SSH.

panels.title: Wi-Fi experience by node
panels.description: 0-100 per Wi-Fi device, worked out by the collector: 50% signal (-90 dBm scores 0, -50 dBm scores full), 30% link rate against what the channel width allows (2-stream Wi-Fi 6), 20% retries since the device connected (half of frames retried scores 0). Above 85 is great, below 50 is a poor link.

panels.title: Sticky clients (weak signal for an hour, no roam)
panels.description: Devices that stayed below -75 dBm for the last hour on the same node. A closer node would serve them better: they hold on to a weak link instead of roaming. Turning Wi-Fi off and on, or moving the node, usually helps.

panels.title: On 2.4 GHz but 5 GHz capable
panels.description: Devices on 2.4 GHz now that have used 5 or 6 GHz before (within the device history). 2.4 GHz is slower and more crowded; these usually end up there from distance or smart-connect band steering.

panels.title: Ping to each device
panels.description: Empty unless `LAN_CLIENT_PING=true` in .env. One ping a minute from the server to each online device on the main LAN. Phones in power-save mode answer late or not at all.

panels.title: Not answering (last 15 min)
panels.description: Online per the router but losing most pings: often a firewall on the device (Windows blocks ping by default), sometimes a bad Wi-Fi link.

options.content:
Full device inventory, new-device alerts and presence history are in **[NetAlertX](http://192.168.50.10:20211)**.

Names come from the Asus app and DHCP. Name devices in the Asus app to make this page easier to read.
